cards.article_text: A 60-year-old man was arrested in connection with a hit-and-run crash that critically injured a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident, police said. The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Ft. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. He said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened. Investigators reviewed video, physical evidence and other leads since the crash two weeks ago. Niemczyk said a geofence warrant which sought cellphone location data from a specific area during a specific time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell phone towers in that area at the time of the crash. That helped detectives identify Aude as the alleged hit and run driver and the vehicles registered to him. Detectives then located and examined the man’s vehicle, which had damage consistent with striking a pedestrian, including damage to the front bumper and hood, Niemczyk said. Investigators also found presumptive positive results for blood on the vehicle. Further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle’s inner fender-well fasteners at the scene, Niemczyk said. Detectives found that several matching fasteners were missing from the suspect’s vehicle. Investigators are still looking for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or if the driver of the second vehicle witnessed the accident. We’re very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we’ve arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred, Niemczyk said. The Police Chief said the victim was in the middle of the road when he was struck, but investigators could not determine from the video whether he was walking or jogging. Police learned he often exercised at night when the weather was cooler and he was known to walk on the road and medians. "I've been doing this for 30 years. I'm not surprised by a whole lot anymore. I've seen pedestrians left for dead on the side of the road before. It doesn't make it any easier, but it doesn't surprise me at this point either. It's just difficult to understand how one human being could be so, you know, without compassion for another," Chief Niemczyk said. See also: 2 arrested in killing of transgender woman Jayla McGee in Belle Glade The victim had no identification or cellphone with him, Niemczyk said. Investigators used data from a Garmin exercise watch he was wearing to trace his route back to his house and were able to identify him. Niemczyk said the victim has significant head trauma and is unable to speak. He is expected to survive, but the chief said his quality of life may not be the same as it was before the crash. "An arrest cannot undo the harm or uncertainty imposed upon a victim, Niemczyk said, but it’s the first step in accountability. Police have not released a description of the southbound vehicle. Anyone with information is asked to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000. Aude is being held on $45,000 bond.

hero.headline: Injury Crash on Florida's Turnpike Backs Up Traffic 2 Miles in Stuart
hero.body:
A crash with injuries on northbound Florida's Turnpike near mile marker 129 in the Stuart area is causing about a 2-mile traffic backup. The crash was reported shortly after 2:15 p.m. Sunday, according to FL511.

FL511 reported the right lane blocked between mile markers 127 and 129 as of 2:46 p.m. Florida Highway Patrol information listed no roadblock in the area.

Drivers should use caution and expect delays on the northbound Turnpike while crews respond. This is a developing story.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, One Year After Brother's Death
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter/paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency said. His death comes one year after his brother, Jarius Hodge, also a firefighter with the district, died after falling ill at work.

Austin Hodge joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. On Saturday morning, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted him from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Fire District called his death "a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," and extended "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time."

Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at Station 3, where he worked. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, people gathered to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. At that gathering, Austin Hodge said of his brother, "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today." In May, another district firefighter, 21-year-old Connor Whitehead, also died, though the cause of his death was not released.

In the hours after Austin Hodge's death, firefighters, the district's Honor Guard and public safety partners gathered to honor him, the fire district said on Facebook. "The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station," the district wrote. "It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another." The district credited the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties with offering "strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves." Condolences also came in from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations with 523 firefighters countywide. Information on memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

cards.headline: Fatal Medical Call on Florida's Turnpike Near Fort Pierce Leaves One Dead
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a medical emergency on Florida's Turnpike near the Fort Pierce Service Plaza early Sunday, and the incident is now listed as a fatality in state crash records.
cards.body:
A medical emergency on Florida's Turnpike near the Fort Pierce Service Plaza in St. Lucie County has been reported as a fatal incident, according to the Florida Highway Patrol crash database. The incident happened Sunday.

St. Lucie County Fire District said in a statement that it received a call at 5:37 a.m. for a medical emergency near mile marker 145 northbound on the Sunshine State Parkway, also known as Florida's Turnpike. At 5:47 a.m., crews called a "full arrest," and the patient was transported to Florida Coast Medical Center in Port St. Lucie.

The Florida Highway Patrol has been asked for additional information about the incident and has not yet responded.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, Second Brother Lost in a Year
hero.body:
A St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter and paramedic died Saturday morning while on duty, marking the second time in just over a year that the department has lost a member of the Hodge family. Austin Hodge, 34, joined the St. Lucie County Fire District on July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. His brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. Jarius Hodge's family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later.

A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies traveled from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning to honor Austin Hodge. People had gathered on May 30 to celebrate what would have been Jarius Hodge's 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. At that gathering, Austin Hodge said of his brother, "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

The losses come after another St. Lucie County firefighter, Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31. A cause of death for Whitehead was not released. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations with 523 firefighters, according to the agency's website. The district said information regarding memorial arrangements and opportunities to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

cards.headline: PSL Police Arrest Newspaper Delivery Driver in NW California Boulevard Hit-and-Run
cards.teaser: Detectives used a geofence warrant and recovered vehicle fragments to arrest a 60-year-old man in a crash that left a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man with critical head injuries. Police are still searching for a second vehicle seen near the scene.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a 60-year-old newspaper delivery driver in connection with a hit-and-run crash earlier this month that left a 63-year-old resident with critical, life-altering head injuries. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened.

Investigators spent two weeks reviewing video, physical evidence and other leads before making the arrest. A geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area and time produced a lead showing Aude's phone had pinged off cell towers in that area at the time of the crash, helping detectives identify him and the vehicles registered to him. When detectives located and examined his vehicle, they found damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood that require further testing. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle's inner fender-well fasteners at the crash scene and found that matching fasteners were missing from Aude's vehicle.

Investigators are still searching for a second vehicle that was traveling southbound near the crash. Niemczyk said distant video showed a vehicle traveling in each direction, but it was difficult to determine what happened. Police are trying to learn whether the second vehicle also struck the victim or whether its driver witnessed the crash. "We're very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we've arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred,

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies, One Year After Brother's Death
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge, 34, died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency confirmed. Hodge was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce and had served with the district since July 17, 2017. His death comes just over a year after his brother, Jarius Hodge, also a firefighter-paramedic with the district, died after falling ill at Station 3.

A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted Austin Hodge from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025, after his family said he came down with the flu, felt weak at work and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. Family and friends gathered on May 30 to mark what would have been Jarius Hodge's 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

Austin Hodge's death marks the third loss of a St. Lucie County firefighter in recent months. Firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31, though the cause of his death was not released. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations and employs 523 firefighters across the county, according to the agency.

The St. Lucie County Fire District called Hodge's death "a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," extending "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." In a Facebook post, the agency said, "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin's family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Condolences also came from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The St. Lucie County Fire District said information on memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

cards.teaser: Detectives used surveillance video and the victim's Garmin watch data to identify Eric Saint Aude as a suspect in the crash near NW University and NW California boulevards.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested Eric Saint Aude in connection with an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old man in critical condition near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. The crash happened around 12:56 a.m. and left the victim unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries.

Police said the victim, who was out exercising at the time, was a familiar sight to officers working the night shift. "Our officers that work night we're used to seeing him out exercising in the evening and he was known to jog, walk in the street medians," Port St. Lucie Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said. The man was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where he remains in critical condition.

Investigators identified the victim using information from his Garmin watch, which was traced back to his home. Detectives then reviewed surveillance video and gathered additional evidence that led them to identify Saint Aude, 60, as a suspect in the crash.

Saint Aude was arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, according to Port St. Lucie police.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce Police: Missing 5-Year-Old Found Dead in Pond Near Portofino Landing
hero.body:
Fort Pierce police say a 5-year-old nonverbal girl who went missing from her apartment complex Saturday was found dead hours later in a nearby pond, with investigators now revealing new details about the search effort, including an attempt to track her location through a tablet she had with her. Mayra Glory Odelus was last seen before noon in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments east of Interstate 95. Her body was discovered in the pond at about 3 p.m., roughly 75 yards from her apartment, about three hours after she was reported missing. Police received the initial report at 11:39 a.m., and family members told officers Mayra was autistic and nonverbal.

She was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair. Officers searched the surrounding area, handed out flyers with her name and photo, and flew drones over the area. Police called in Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office dive team, which conducted an underwater search that led to the discovery of her body. According to police spokesperson Michael Santiago, Mayra had a tablet with her when she disappeared, and her family tried to locate her by pinging the device. The ping led searchers to the pond area, but at that point there was no sign of her, and the tablet itself has still not been recovered.

Mayra's father told police the pond sits directly across from their apartment and that she loved the water. He and Mayra's 18-year-old sister were home at the time she went missing. Her mother lives in Haiti and was expected to arrive Sunday. "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra's family and loved ones during this tragic time," the Fort Pierce Police Department said in a statement. Santiago added, "It's very tragic when anything like this happens, but with our kids we have to make sure we're paying attention all the time, especially when kids are challenged with autism."

Drowning remains the leading cause of unintentional death among children ages 1 to 3. Dr. Elizabeth Feldman of Cleveland Clinic Florida has said drowning can happen within seconds, and a lack of oxygen for just a few minutes can cause brain injury. The Children's Services Council of Palm Beach reported that 39 children with autism or suspected autism drowned in Florida in 2025, the highest number ever recorded in the state. The case has renewed attention on tracking and safety devices designed to prevent or respond to water-related emergencies involving children with autism, many of whom are drawn to water and may wander from supervision without being able to call for help.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty, Year After Brother's Death
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge, a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic who publicly pushed for medical malpractice accountability after his brother's 2025 death, died while on duty Saturday.
cards.body:
A St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic died while on duty Saturday morning, more than a year after his younger brother, who also served as a firefighter-paramedic for the district, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced the line-of-duty death of Austin Hodge on Saturday, Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge's death have not been released. The fire district asked the public to respect his family's privacy as they grieve and said information about memorial arrangements will be shared once finalized.

Austin Hodge's death comes more than a year after his younger brother, Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. He said his brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, but died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating Jarius, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said his brother had been healthy before becoming ill.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for his brother's death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," he said. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District said additional information about ways to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies, Second Brother Lost in 15 Months
hero.body:
A St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter-paramedic died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency said, marking the second time in just over a year that the department has lost a member of the same family in the line of service. Austin Hodge, 34, had served with the district since July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. His brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. Jarius Hodge's family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later.

Following Austin Hodge's death, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted him from HCA Lawnwood Hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning. The St. Lucie County Fire District said the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties all provided support in the hours after his death. Several other agencies offered condolences, including Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue.

"His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," the agency said in a statement. "The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." In a Facebook post, the district wrote, "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another.

"Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin's family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Austin Hodge had spoken publicly about his brother after Jarius Hodge's death, calling him "a quiet leader" and saying, "He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient." Information on memorial arrangements for Austin Hodge will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations and employs 523 firefighters countywide.

hero.headline: Martin County Approves School Zone for Citrus Grove Elementary After 5-Year Push
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners have unanimously approved a new school zone on Southwest Newfield Parkway outside Citrus Grove Elementary School, answering years of safety concerns from parents who say the current 45 mph speed limit puts children at risk. Many families whose children walk to school live in the Canopy Creek community across the street from the elementary school.

Kelly Ribaudo, the school's PTA president and Martin County PTA Advocacy Chair, said she has spent the last five years asking the county to install a school zone. "We've had so many near misses with the kids just from people not paying attention," Ribaudo said. "Everyone has a right to a free and public education and they should be safe getting there. Our main priority should be the kids not the traffic." Parent Kendall George said the current traffic conditions are frightening. "It scares me," George said. "These cars are driving 45 miles an hour plus."

At a previous Martin County Commission meeting, commissioners sided with the parents. "Whatever the number is there is no price to someone getting hurt," Martin County Commissioner Edward Ciampi said. "You will absolutely get a school zone." School Principal Rose Rynca said the need has grown as new communities have developed in the area and enrollment has increased. "The amount of students crossing Newfield Parkway has definitely increased," Rynca said. "This speed zone is going to really really improve the safety of students." George said a marked school zone will help remind drivers to be careful. "It's letting drivers know that, hey there's a school here, there's children crossing, and we have to slow down," George said.

The county was asked this week for a timeline on when the school zone will be installed on Southwest Newfield Parkway. In the meantime, parents are urging drivers to use caution near the school regardless of posted signage. "Slow down if you see a school, even if there's not a school zone sign, slow down," Ribaudo said. With the school zone now approved, parents say their next priority is pushing the county for improved street lighting in the area.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies, Brother Died in Same Job in 2025
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge, a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic for more than nine years, died in the line of duty Saturday, just over a year after his younger brother Jarius died while serving in the same department.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius, who also served as a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced Hodge's death on Saturday, Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9. Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue also shared condolences following his unexpected death Saturday morning. The circumstances surrounding Austin Hodge's death have not been released.

Austin Hodge's death comes more than a year after his brother Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025. Austin said his younger brother went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22, struggling to breathe, and died hours later. He alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill.

Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius's death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He emphasized that his family was seeking accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable." The St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect the Hodge family as they grieve and said information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Austin Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family once details are finalized.

hero.body:
A 5-year-old nonverbal girl who went missing from the Portofino Landing Apartments in Fort Pierce was found dead in a nearby pond three hours later, and Fort Pierce police on Saturday released new details about the search that preceded the discovery. Mayra Glory Odelus was last seen before noon in the 5100 block of Portofino Landing Apartments, east of Interstate 95. Her body was found in the pond at about 3 p.m.

Fort Pierce police spokesperson Michael Santiago said officers received the report of the missing girl at 11:39 a.m. Family members told police Mayra was autistic and nonverbal. Officers searched the surrounding area, distributed flyers with her name and photo, and launched drones. Police also requested help from Port St. Lucie bloodhounds and a dive team from the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office. Mayra was last seen wearing a dark oversized shirt with two white beads in her hair. In a 4:15 p.m. update, Fort Pierce police wrote, "Our deepest condolences are with Mayra's family and loved ones during this tragic time."

Santiago said Mayra had a tablet with her when she disappeared, and her family was able to ping the device in an effort to locate her. "One of the interesting things about this is that she actually had a tablet with her and the family was able to ping the tablet to try and locate where she was," Santiago said. Her mother, who lives in Haiti, was expected to arrive Sunday.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Mourns Second Hodge Brother in a Year
hero.body:
A firefighter-paramedic with the St. Lucie County Fire District died Saturday morning while on duty, just over a year after his brother, also a member of the department, died in similar circumstances. Austin Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, and served the community for more than nine years. He was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce.

Austin's brother, Jarius Hodge, died on July 22, 2025, after falling ill at work at Station 3. His family said he had the flu, felt weak and was later rushed to the hospital, where he died hours later. On May 30, friends and family gathered for a cookout and balloon release to celebrate what would have been Jarius's 27th birthday. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

On Saturday, a procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies escorted Austin Hodge from the hospital to the morgue in Fort Pierce. The St. Lucie County Fire District, which operates 20 fire stations with 523 firefighters, said in a statement that his death "is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community" and extended "heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." The district said information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor Hodge's service will be shared in coordination with his family as details are finalized.

The department also thanked agencies across the region for their support in the hours after the loss. In a Facebook post, the district wrote, "In the hours following this heartbreaking loss, our firefighters, Honor Guard, and public safety partners came together to honor our fallen brother and stand alongside one another during an incredibly difficult time. The brotherhood of the fire service extends far beyond the walls of a fire station. It is a bond built on trust, shared experiences, and an unwavering commitment to one another. Today, that bond was especially evident through the incredible support of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office, Fort Pierce Police Department, Port St. Lucie Police Department, and peer support teams from Martin and Indian River counties. Together, they offered strength, compassion, and support while ensuring Austin was honored with the dignity and respect he deserves. Our hearts are with Austin's family, loved ones, and everyone who had the privilege of serving alongside him. We are deeply grateful to our fellow first responders and community for the outpouring of support during this tremendous loss." Condolences also came from Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, Indian River County Emergency Services Department, Indian River County Fire Rescue, Palm Beach County Fire Rescue and Riviera Beach Fire Rescue. The district also lost firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, who died on May 31.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies On Duty A Year After Brother's Death
cards.teaser: Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, 15 months after his younger brother Jarius died following treatment at Cleveland Clinic Tradition in Port St. Lucie. Austin had publicly pushed for accountability over his brother's death and criticized Florida's medical malpractice laws.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic Austin Hodge died while on duty Saturday, more than a year after his younger brother Jarius, also a St. Lucie County firefighter-paramedic, died at age 26. The St. Lucie County Fire District announced Hodge's line-of-duty death on Oct. 24, calling it a profound loss to the department and the fire service community. Hodge joined the district on July 17, 2017, served the community for more than nine years, and was assigned to Station 9. The circumstances surrounding his death have not been released.

Neighboring Indian River County Fire Rescue shared condolences following Hodge's unexpected death Saturday morning. The St. Lucie County Fire District asked the public to respect Hodge's family as they grieve and said additional information about memorial arrangements and ways to honor his service will be shared in coordination with the family once finalized.

Hodge's death comes more than a year after his brother Jarius Hodge died on July 22, 2025. The brothers shared a close bond and a passion for serving their community. "We had the same hairstyle." He described Jarius as someone who loved his family and his work as a first responder. "He loved going to work, loved working beside me. I loved working beside him," Austin said. "He always pushed me to keep going. He was someone who loved his family, his community and his country."

In that earlier interview, Austin said Jarius became ill after catching the flu from a patient at work in July 2025 and went to Cleveland Clinic Tradition Hospital in Port St. Lucie on July 22 struggling to breathe, but died hours later. Austin alleged that medical staff made critical errors in treating his brother, including taking three attempts to intubate him, and said Jarius had been healthy before becoming ill. Austin also spoke publicly about Florida's medical malpractice laws, arguing that restrictions on who can pursue certain wrongful-death claims prevented his family from seeking legal accountability for Jarius' death. "This is unjust, and it's been going on for too long," Austin said. He emphasized that his family sought accountability rather than financial compensation. "For me personally, for my family, this has nothing to do with any type of dollar," he said. "We just want those physicians to be held accountable."

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District Firefighter Austin Hodge Dies on Duty in Fort Pierce
hero.teaser: Austin Hodge, a nine-year veteran assigned to Station 9, died Saturday morning just over a year after his brother Jarius Hodge died while on duty with the same district.
hero.body:
A St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter and paramedic died Saturday morning while on duty, the agency said. Austin Hodge had served the district for more than nine years after joining on July 17, 2017, and was assigned to Station 9 in Fort Pierce. A procession of firefighters and personnel from other agencies left the morgue in Fort Pierce on Saturday morning following his death.

Hodge's death comes just over a year after his brother, Jarius Hodge, also a St. Lucie County Fire District firefighter, died on July 22, 2025. Jarius Hodge fell ill at work at Station 3, where his family said he had flu symptoms and felt weak before being rushed to the hospital. He died there hours later. Friends and family gathered on May 30 to celebrate what would have been his 27th birthday with a cookout and balloon release. At that event, Austin Hodge said of his brother, "He was a quiet leader, and we take a lot from him. He was my younger brother, but I looked up to him in many ways to keep me poised, keep me patient. And I think that's what he's teaching everybody today."

The district has faced other losses in recent months. Firefighter Connor Whitehead, 21, died on May 31. The St. Lucie County Fire District operates 20 fire stations and employs 523 firefighters, according to the agency's website.

"His death is a profound loss to the St. Lucie County Fire District and the fire service community," the district said in a statement. "The District extends its heartfelt condolences to Hodge's family, friends, and fellow firefighters during this difficult time." Several agencies offered condolences following Austin Hodge's death, including Port St. Lucie Fire Rescue, the Fort Pierce Police Officers Association, the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the Indian River County Sheriff's Office, the Indian River County Emergency Services Department and Indian River County Fire Rescue.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Man in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Jogger
hero.teaser: Detectives used surveillance video and the victim's Garmin watch data to identify a suspect in the hit-and-run that left a 63-year-old man with severe head injuries. Eric Saint Aude, 60, has been arrested on a charge of leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury.
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a man in connection with an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old jogger critically injured. Eric Saint Aude, 60, was taken into custody and charged with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

The crash happened around 12:56 a.m. near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. Officers found the 63-year-old man unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries. He was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital and remains in critical condition.

Investigators identified the victim using information from his Garmin watch, which they traced back to his home. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said night-shift officers were familiar with the victim from his regular exercise routine. "Our officers that work night we're used to seeing him out exercising in the evening and he was known to jog, walk in the street medians," Niemczyk said.

Detectives reviewed surveillance video along with additional evidence to identify Saint Aude as a suspect in the crash. That investigative work led to his arrest on the hit-and-run charge, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department.

hero.body:
A newly released Florida Highway Patrol report details how a 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday when the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. The traffic homicide investigation remains open, and the man's next of kin had not been notified as of the report.

According to the crash report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street and attempted to turn left when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner did not report any injuries.

Florida Highway Patrol's traffic homicide investigation into the crash is ongoing.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
hero.teaser: Detectives traced a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers before linking it to a 22-year-old New York man.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old man from the Bronx has been extradited to St. Lucie County to face charges after detectives linked him to a check stolen from a Port St. Lucie real estate company and funneled through a money laundering scheme, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo faces charges of money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft.

The Sheriff's Office Economic Crimes Unit launched a multi-jurisdictional investigation after a check mailed by the Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen and fraudulently altered. The check was deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity, according to the Sheriff's Office. Detectives then traced the money as it moved through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers, which investigators say were used to disguise where the funds originated, before the money landed in Diallo's personal bank account.

Diallo was apprehended on Oct. 14 by Canadian border authorities as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond was set at a total of $30,000 across the three charges.

"Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

Lucie County Sheriff’s Office Economic Crimes Unit conducted a multi-jurisdictional investigation, culminating in the arrest of Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx. A check mailed by a Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered, and deposited into a bank account established using a stolen identity, the sheriff's office said. cards.headline: St. Lucie Fire District Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee in 4-3 Vote
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. The board appointed Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief following the decision.

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. The disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel said he sees his new role as a chance to move the department forward. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics," he said.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated in the hazing case, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. The question of whether the three fired firefighters could be reinstated remains unresolved as Langel settles into his new role.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Mayor's Race, Trash Pickup Question Top Nov. Ballot
hero.body:
Early voting is underway in Port St. Lucie, where voters will decide a tense mayoral race between incumbent Shannon Martin and challenger Steven Giordano, along with a non-binding ballot question asking whether the city should switch to twice-a-week trash pickup, a change that would cost residents more than $100 a year. Election day is less than two weeks away.

On the first day of early voting, campaign tents for Martin and Giordano stood side by side outside a polling location on Rosser Boulevard, reflecting what has become a bitter contest. Martin is running for another term and argues the city should stay on its current course, pointing to infrastructure work, including roadwork, as evidence her administration is delivering results. Giordano has accused City Hall of corruption and of losing touch with everyday residents. When asked what he would do differently, he also pointed to roadwork, saying the city needs a new traffic study. Port St. Lucie's mayor serves a four-year term and holds significant power under the city's mayor-council form of government. Neither candidate is running with a party affiliation, since the mayoral race is nonpartisan.

The ballot also asks voters whether the city should add a second weekly trash collection day. FCC handles garbage collection in Port St. Lucie. The question will not bind the city council, which could choose to ignore the outcome regardless of how residents vote. At recent city council meetings, residents have complained that current trash service is inadequate and have pushed for an additional pickup day. Resident Rob Buske offered a different view, saying, "I don't want to pay for something I don't need." On the first day of early voting, people asked about the issue said they would rather keep the current one-day pickup schedule, even as others have demanded a change.

The trash question, like the mayoral race, is nonpartisan, but both issues have generated strong feelings among residents. The choice over who leads the city comes down to differing visions for Port St. Lucie's direction, while the trash question centers on a simpler, more immediate concern: how often garbage gets picked up at the curb. Both items will appear on the same ballot as voters decide the city's near-term direction over the next two weeks.

hero.headline: Leon County probe: CBP agents at polling site tried to vote, not enforce
hero.body:
Leon County election officials and the FBI have concluded that Customs and Border Protection agents seen near an early voting site this week were mistakenly trying to vote before leaving the state, not conducting an immigration enforcement action. A separate incident involving an armed arrest near a Key Largo polling place remains under review by Monroe County election officials. Both episodes drew scrutiny because federal law bars armed officers or troops from operating near polling places, and the Trump administration has repeatedly assured election officials that federal agents would not be stationed at voting sites.

The Leon County incident began Monday when two CBP vehicles parked outside the Northeast Branch Library, described by county election supervisor Mark Earley as the busiest early voting site in the county. The vehicles stayed about 10 minutes before leaving. Earley said his office received no calls from voters about the incident, but he filed a complaint with the FBI because voters may experience intimidation. On Friday, Earley's office said the county sheriff's office and FBI determined the vehicles belonged to a team of agents normally stationed in south Florida who had been reassigned to another state. While driving north to their new post, they stopped at the last Florida polling place on their route after realizing they would not be in the state on Election Day. Earley said the agents mistakenly believed they could vote there, even though they were not Leon County voters, and left immediately once they learned otherwise. He said he accepts that account and considers it an isolated incident consistent with assurances that federal agents would not be stationed at polling sites.

A CBP spokesperson said the officers were traveling in a government vehicle from Florida to Brownsville, Texas, in support of an out-of-state deployment, and that the stop was not an immigration enforcement action. hero.headline: PSLPD Arrest in NW California Boulevard Hit-and-Run, Second Vehicle Sought
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a man in connection with the Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie resident in critical condition, and investigators are still trying to identify a second vehicle that may have also been involved. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested 60-year-old Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. Aude is being held on $45,000 bond.

The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on Oct. 9 on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the road with severe head injuries and remains at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Niemczyk said Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash happened.

Detectives built the case using video, physical evidence and other leads gathered over the two weeks since the crash. A geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area at the time of the collision showed Aude's phone had pinged off cell towers there, which helped investigators identify him and the vehicles registered to him. When detectives examined Aude's vehicle, they found damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood, though further testing is needed. Police also recovered pieces of an inner fender-well fastener at the scene and found that matching fasteners were missing from Aude's vehicle.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
hero.teaser: A 22-year-old New York man faces felony charges after detectives traced a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through a multi-state money laundering scheme.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old New York man is facing felony charges in St. Lucie County after detectives said they traced a stolen and altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through a web of bank accounts and Zelle transfers. The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office announced Friday that Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx, was arrested following a multi-jurisdictional investigation by the agency's Economic Crimes Unit.

According to the sheriff's office, a check mailed by the Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered, and deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity. Detectives said they traced the stolen funds as they moved through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers allegedly used to hide where the money came from, before it was ultimately deposited into Diallo's personal bank account.

Detectives obtained an arrest warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft. On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he tried to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond was set at a total of $30,000 across the three charges.

"Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police: Two Vehicles May Have Hit Man in Fatal Crash
cards.teaser: Investigators now believe a 63-year-old man found unconscious near Northwest University Boulevard was struck by two separate vehicles, and police have released new images seeking help identifying both drivers.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police have updated their investigation into an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old Port St. Lucie man seriously injured, now saying two vehicles may have struck him rather than one. Detectives believe the victim was hit near the intersection of Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard by one vehicle traveling northbound and another traveling southbound.

The crash happened at approximately 12:56 a.m., when the man was found unconscious in the roadway suffering from severe head injuries. In an earlier update, police said surveillance video from a nearby business captured the incident and showed what investigators believed was a white four-door sedan striking the man before fleeing the scene without stopping.

As detectives continued reviewing evidence and surveillance footage, they developed information indicating a second vehicle may also have been involved in the crash. Police are now working to identify both vehicles and their drivers and have released images of the vehicles to the public.

Anyone who recognizes either vehicle, was in the area at the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or surveillance video from the area is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Lee, Names Langel Interim Chief
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 on Thursday to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, ending months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The board appointed Paul Langel, who has 30 years of experience in the district, as interim chief.

The vote comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. Those disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel said he sees his new role as a chance to move the department forward after a turbulent stretch. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the terminated firefighters could eventually get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics," he said.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated over the hazing allegations, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. The board's action marks a significant shift in a controversy that has consumed the fire district for months, and it now falls to Langel to steer the department through its next chapter.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Killed in Thursday Crash With Semi-Truck in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday morning after his SUV collided with a semi-truck at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in unincorporated Indian River County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 6:45 a.m.

FHP said a Freightliner semi-truck was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street and attempting to turn left onto 66th Avenue. At the same time, a Dodge Durango was traveling north in the inside lane of 66th Avenue, which had no traffic controls at that intersection. Troopers said the Freightliner entered the path of the SUV, and the front of the Durango struck the left side of the semi-trailer. Both vehicles came to rest in the area of the collision.

The driver of the SUV, the 60-year-old Vero Beach man, was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne. He was pronounced dead just after 8 a.m., according to FHP. The driver of the Freightliner, a 59-year-old Jacksonville man, was not injured in the crash.

The crash remains under investigation by the Florida Highway Patrol.

cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Chief Jeff Lee without cause following a hazing scandal and a no-confidence vote. The board named 30-year veteran Paul Langel as interim chief.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

The board appointed Paul Langel as interim chief. Langel has 30 years of experience in the district. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs. The disciplined firefighters have called their terminations retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership. Jordon Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, said of Lee's ouster, "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department."

Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel said he was not ready to commit to an outcome. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

cards.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud Scheme
cards.teaser: A 22-year-old New York man was arrested near the Canadian border and extradited to St. Lucie County on charges connected to a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company.
cards.body:
A 22-year-old man from New York is facing money laundering and fraud charges after detectives say he helped funnel stolen money from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through a chain of bank accounts, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said Friday. Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx, was extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. following a multi-jurisdictional investigation by the sheriff's office Economic Crimes Unit.

Investigators said a check mailed by the Port St. Lucie real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered and deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity. Detectives traced the money through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers that were allegedly used to hide where it came from before it landed in Diallo's personal bank account.

Detectives obtained a warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more, and grand theft. On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he attempted to cross from the United States into Canada. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County. Bond was set at a total of $30,000 for the three charges.

St. Lucie County Sheriff Richard Del Toro credited the Economic Crimes Unit for tracking down the suspect. "Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Water Tank Mural Named National Tank of the Year
cards.teaser: The painted water storage tank at Jaycee Park in Fort Pierce has won Tnemec Company's 2026 Tank of the Year contest, beating out 11 other finalists nationwide. Artist Christian Stanley and Fort Pierce Utilities Authority celebrated the honor.
cards.body:
A water storage tank at Jaycee Park in Fort Pierce has been named the winner of the 2026 Tank of the Year contest, an annual competition run by Tnemec Company, Inc., a maker of high-performance coatings. The company announced the winner and its Top 12 finalists on Friday, selecting the Fort Pierce tank over entries from across the country, including Detroit Lakes, Minnesota, which won the separate People's Choice award.

The tank features a mural by Christian Stanley of C. Stanley Creative showing sea turtles, dolphins, manatees, pelicans and tropical fish, turning the ground storage tank into a tribute to Florida's coastal environment and wildlife. The structure is coated with Tnemec's Series 1026 Enduratone product. Tnemec said a panel of water tank enthusiasts judged entries on artistic value, significance to the community and the challenges involved in completing each project.

Stanley, who grew up in Stuart, said he learned of the win from his sales representative. "Pretty excited," Stanley said. "I got the call earlier from our sales rep. He was excited to share that we were the first-place winner of Tnemec's Tank of the Year. And yeah, we're just beyond excited, and I'm excited to share that with them and with the community that they have an award-winning piece of public art there in their community." Stanley and his wife, Jessica, traveled from Central Florida to apply a UV clear coat to the tank. He said the project carries extra meaning because of his ties to the area. "We were runners-up in 2024, and that was exciting," he said. "But I was like, man, I really want to try. And I know we can make something that would win the first-place award. So, it's, you know, taken a couple of years for us to get there. But I'm excited that we were able to come some bring something together and that Fort Pierce trusted us to make something that we felt was going to be really impactful and iconic for the community there." He added, "I grew up in Stuart, so it was great to visit kind of my old hometown and just be back in the community and be a part of it again, and to kind of leave a footprint. This thing will kind of continue to have a life of its own beyond just the just the tank. And it'll have a bigger footprint than even what we could anticipate. So, it's really cool to get some recognition for the for the award. And we're excited to see what comes next from this."

Fort Pierce Utilities Authority credited its collaboration with Stanley and the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency this summer for transforming the tank into a local landmark. "We are thrilled and deeply grateful to receive the Tank of the Year award," the utility said in a statement attributed to Rachel Tennant, FPUA Director of Public Affairs Sustainability. "Thank you to everyone who voted and supported us, and to the teams who made it happen. It has been an absolute pleasure and honor for our team here at FPUA to collaborate with the artist and the Fort Pierce Redevelopment Agency this summer, turning the Jaycee Park Water Tank into a Fort Pierce landmark." Kevin Morris, Tnemec's director of sales for the water tank market, said the contest has run for 20 years and praised this year's entries. "Fort Pierce is a great example of how a water tank can become more than a functional structure," Morris said. "It can become a landmark that residents are proud to call their own." The Fort Pierce tank will appear as the January image in Tnemec's 2027 water tank calendar, alongside the other finalists and nominees from the contest.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud, Money Laundering Case
hero.teaser: A 22-year-old New York man was extradited to St. Lucie County after detectives traced a stolen, altered check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company through multiple bank accounts. He faces money laundering, scheme to defraud and grand theft charges with bond set at $30,000.
hero.body:
A 22-year-old man from New York is facing money laundering and fraud charges after the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said he took part in a scheme that targeted a Port St. Lucie real estate company. The sheriff's office said its Economic Crimes Unit conducted a multi-jurisdictional investigation that led to the arrest of Gibrill Diallo, of the Bronx.

According to the sheriff's office, a check mailed by the real estate company was stolen, fraudulently altered and deposited into a bank account that had been set up using a stolen identity. Detectives said they traced the stolen funds through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers allegedly used to hide where the money came from before it was ultimately deposited into Diallo's personal bank account.

Detectives obtained an arrest warrant charging Diallo with money laundering between $300 and $20,000, scheme to defraud $50,000 or more, and grand theft. On Oct. 14, Canadian border authorities apprehended Diallo as he attempted to enter Canada from the United States. He was held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before being extradited to St. Lucie County on Wednesday at 9:39 p.m. Bond was set at $30,000 total for the three charges.

"Our detectives followed the money, uncovered a complex financial scheme, and pursued every lead until the suspect was brought back to St. Lucie County to face justice," Sheriff Richard Del Toro said in a statement. "This case reflects the relentless investigative work and determination of our Economic Crimes Unit. Our residents and businesses work hard for what they earn, and they deserve to know that when someone tries to take advantage of them, our detectives will go the extra mile to hold those responsible accountable."

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee Without Cause
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee after months of hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote, naming 30-year veteran Paul Langel as interim chief.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The board named Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief following the vote.

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appeared to show the alleged hazing, and three of the firefighters involved ultimately lost their jobs. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

Langel addressed his new role after the board's vote. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the firefighters terminated over the bug-zapper incident could get their jobs back, Langel said, "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics."

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the firefighters terminated in connection with the hazing scandal, said he saw the board's decision on Lee as a positive step for the department. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. The disciplined firefighters have called the termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Suspect in Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Pedestrian
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a 60-year-old man in connection with a hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old resident critically injured earlier this month. Police Chief Leo Niemczyk said detectives arrested Eric Saint Aude on Oct. 22 and charged him with leaving the scene of a crash involving serious bodily injury. The crash happened shortly before 1 a.m. on NW California Boulevard just south of the intersection with NW University Boulevard, leaving the victim unconscious in the road with severe head injuries. He remains in critical condition at HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in Fort Pierce. Niemczyk said Saint Aude was working as a newspaper delivery driver and was on his way to pick up newspapers when the crash occurred.

Investigators spent two weeks reviewing video footage, physical evidence and other leads before making the arrest. A geofence warrant seeking cellphone location data from the crash area during the time of the incident showed that Saint Aude's phone had pinged off nearby cell towers, which led detectives to him and to vehicles registered in his name. When they located and examined his vehicle, they found damage to the front bumper and hood consistent with striking a pedestrian, along with presumptive positive results for blood that still require further testing. Police also recovered pieces of the vehicle's inner fender-well fasteners at the scene and discovered that matching fasteners were missing from Saint Aude's vehicle. "We're very confident that the vehicle that we have and the person that we've arrested are responsible for the majority of what occurred," Niemczyk said.

Investigators are still trying to locate a second vehicle that was seen traveling southbound near the crash site. Niemczyk said distant video captured vehicles moving in each direction, but it was not clear enough to determine exactly what happened. Police want to know whether that second vehicle also struck the victim or simply witnessed the crash. Niemczyk said the victim was in the middle of the road when he was hit, though investigators could not tell from the video whether he had been walking or jogging. He added that the man frequently exercised at night and was known to walk along the road and its medians. Police have not released a description of the second vehicle and are asking anyone with information to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

The victim had no identification or cellphone on him when he was found, but investigators used data from a Garmin exercise watch he was wearing to trace his route home and identify him. Niemczyk said the man suffered significant head trauma and is currently unable to speak. He is expected to survive, though the chief said his quality of life may not return to what it was before the crash. "It's just difficult to understand how one human being could be so, you know, without compassion for another," Niemczyk said.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee After Hazing Scandal
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. The board also voted to appoint Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief.

The firing comes two months after five firefighters were displaced amid allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three of those firefighters ultimately lost their jobs. The disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction," Hutchinson said. "I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department."

Langel said he sees his new role as a chance to move the department forward after a turbulent stretch. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process." Asked whether the terminated firefighters could eventually get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics." Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation under his contract, which ends early as a result of the board's vote.

hero.headline: Bronx Man Extradited to St. Lucie County in Check Fraud Case After Border Arrest
hero.body:
A 20-year-old Bronx, New York, man has been extradited to St. Lucie County after Canadian border authorities arrested him as he tried to enter Canada, the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office said. Gibrill Diallo faces charges of money laundering, a scheme to defraud of $50,000 or more and grand theft in connection with a stolen check from a Port St. Lucie real estate company.

The Sheriff's Office said the check was altered and deposited into a bank account opened using a stolen identity. Detectives traced the funds through multiple bank accounts and Zelle transfers before they were deposited into Diallo's personal bank account.

Diallo was arrested Oct. 21 and held at the Niagara County Jail in New York before his extradition. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said detectives followed the money and pursued leads across jurisdictions to build the case.
