hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee, Taxpayers Face $350,000 Severance
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire Board voted Wednesday to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee's contract without cause, ending his tenure with a severance package expected to total about $350,000. The firing follows a no-confidence vote among union firefighters, in which more than 74% of those who participated said they had no confidence in Lee.

The vote capped months of fallout from a hazing investigation into videos involving firefighters at Station 1A. Some videos showed a modified bug zapper being used to shock three apprentice firefighters while on duty in 2024. Others showed water being dumped on two firefighters and a dead raccoon placed inside a fire vehicle. A third-party investigator concluded the videos depicted hazing, and veteran firefighters Doug Boudrias, Jordan Hutchinson and Chris Baldwin were fired as a result, though all three disputed that characterization and said the incidents were consensual pranks. "It was just us in our downtime, joking around, having fun," Hutchinson said. "We're all still friends," Boudrias added. Their firings drew outcry from firefighters, former firefighters and community members, many of whom packed the Fire Administration building Wednesday holding signs or wearing shirts in support of the three men. "Not only have they lost their jobs, but they also lost their reputations," one public commentator said.

St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire Board member Jamie Fowler said the decision to remove Lee was not about a single misstep. "At the end of the day, it's gotten very messy. It's not about one single decision that he's made. It's about bringing peace and calm and respect back to the district and the men and women that serve this community every day, and it just got to a point where he was not effective anymore," Fowler said. Fire Board member and business owner Travis Leonard made the motion to fire Lee, pointing to a letter Lee had sent the board days earlier suggesting it may be time for a "mutually agreeable retirement and leadership transition" because "the position of fire chief requires confidence." "Coming from the private sector, anytime an employee gives their notice, I terminate them; I found they've checked out," Leonard said. St. Lucie County Commissioner and Fire Board member James Clasby said the vote reflected what the union's no-confidence poll had already shown. "There was a large desire to have a change in leadership, and we delivered that today," Clasby said.

After terminating Lee's contract, the board appointed Deputy Chief Paul Langel as interim fire chief. The district also plans to hire a recruiter to search for Lee's permanent replacement. "I am excited to move this district forward, to begin the healing process of the issues that we've been dealing with, as of recent, and to instill trust," Langel said.

The leadership shakeup comes as the firefighters union continues negotiating with the district to reinstate Boudrias, Hutchinson and Baldwin. Union Representative Ryan Sapp called Lee's termination a "positive step forward." "I think moving forward, the ultimate goal here is to just move forward and get things back to a level field and continue providing the services to our community," Sapp said. "The biggest thing today is we worked together and came together as a local, glad to see my membership stepped up and let their voices be heard." The union vote also showed about 92% of firefighters had no confidence in Assistant Chief Brian Gonzalez and 97% had no confidence in District Attorney Kim Sabol, who has submitted her notice of retirement amid the controversy. The Fire Board is now searching for her replacement as well.

The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The board immediately appointed Paul Langel, a 30-year veteran of the district, as interim chief.

"I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

The board's decision comes two months after five firefighters were displaced over allegations they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three of the firefighters were ultimately terminated. Jordon Hutchinson, one of the fired firefighters, called the board's vote on Lee a step in the right direction. "I don't think today was about us by any means," Hutchinson said. "I think it was the best thing for the entire department." The disciplined firefighters have said their terminations were retaliation for complaints they had previously filed against district leadership.

Asked whether the terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel said he was not ready to make that call. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics." Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Arrest Suspect in Hit-and-Run That Critically Injured Resident
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police have arrested a suspect in a hit-and-run crash that left a 63-year-old resident critically injured earlier this month. The crash happened about 12:56 a.m. on the 9th near NW University Boulevard and NW California Boulevard. The victim was found unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital, where the victim remained in critical condition.

Detectives reviewed surveillance video and gathered additional evidence while working to identify the vehicle or vehicles involved and those who left the scene. As of Thursday, investigators believed they were looking for two vehicles.

Police planned to release more information at a news conference scheduled for 1 p.m. Friday at department headquarters. The suspect's identity and any charges had not been released.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man, 60, Dies in Crash at 66th Avenue and 49th Street
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. The Florida Highway Patrol said a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was turning left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the crash report.

The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner reported no injuries.

hero.headline: 86-Year-Old Found Dead After Car Plunges Into Indian River Lagoon in Vero Beach
hero.body:
An 86-year-old man was found dead inside a car pulled from the Indian River Lagoon in Vero Beach after witnesses said the vehicle drove through a fence at a condo complex and into the water. Police have not yet identified the man. Authorities said he had gone missing the night before the car was discovered.

Residents at the condo complex said they knew the driver. Tire marks were visible near the scene where the car breached the fence before entering the lagoon. Police worked for hours to pull the silver Honda CR-V from the water as the investigation got underway.

The crash left a visible mark on the community. Residents on Greytwig Road were later seen cleaning up the parking lot, removing mud and scrubbing away tire marks left behind. Several described the scene as unsettling.

Police have not released the identity of the victim and continue to investigate what led up to the crash. The case remains active as authorities work to determine the circumstances that caused the vehicle to leave the roadway and enter the lagoon.

cards.headline: Red Flag Warning Keeps St. Lucie Beaches Under High Hazard Advisory
cards.teaser: Four to six foot surf and rip current risk prompted St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers toward lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach.
cards.body:
A red flag warning has put St. Lucie County beaches under a high hazard advisory, with waves between four and six feet crashing along the shoreline at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park on Wednesday. The dangerous surf and rip current risk prompted St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers to head to lifeguarded beaches such as Pepper Park and Waveland Beach, where officials say red or double red flags will likely keep flying for the next few days.

Fort Pierce Inlet State Park was among several St. Lucie County beaches under the red flag warning, which officials tied to a low pressure system off the eastern United States coast in the mid-Atlantic. Fort Pierce resident Lee Bertucelli described the water conditions bluntly. "The sea was angry today my friends," he said.

The rough surf made for challenging conditions for people in the water. "It was very windy and very choppy and it's really challenging because you have to negotiate all of the chop," foil surfer Lisa Rose said. Surfer Jodi Riley said she only ventured in to her waist rather than bringing her surfboard. "I went in, not with my surfboard, but like, to my waist and it's just, it's rough and it's just not super safe for like, I'm sort of a beginner so not safe for me, but like, some of the other surfers have definitely been out," Riley said.

Bertucelli said he stayed cautious despite enjoying the waves. "I went in, you know, not too far. The waves were fun, but again not too far, didn't want to deal with rip tides or anything else," he said. St. Lucie County officials say rip currents are possible under these conditions and advise swimmers caught in one not to panic and to swim parallel to the shoreline. Ocean Rescue continues to stress that lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach are the safest option while the red flag advisory remains in effect.

hero.headline: Veterans Golf Free as Tee It Up for the Troops Debuts at Lost Lake in Hobe Sound
hero.body:
A Veterans Day golf tournament is bringing paying players together with local veterans, who will golf for free, when Tee It Up for the Troops holds its event for the first time at The Club at Lost Lake in Hobe Sound on Wednesday, Nov. 11. The field is capped at 106 golfers, with registration priced at $750 per player, and veterans paired into foursomes will not pay to play.

Chris LaRocque, president and executive director of Tee It Up for the Troops, said the cause is personal. "It's very close to my heart," LaRocque said in an ARC Florida interview. "I'm an Army Reserve major myself." He said the nonprofit has deployed more than $20 million and supported more than 400,000 veterans through programs that help with the transition to civilian jobs and provide support for post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injuries.

Proceeds from the Hobe Sound tournament will also support local veterans programs, including PGA HOPE in South Florida, LaRocque said. PGA HOPE introduces veterans and active-duty service members to golf as a way to support their physical, mental, social and emotional well-being.

The tournament will take place at The Club at Lost Lake, 8300 SE Fazio Drive in Hobe Sound. Registration and event information are available through Tee It Up for the Troops.

hero.headline: Martin County Commission Approves School Zone for Citrus Grove Elementary
hero.body:
Martin County commissioners have unanimously approved a new school zone on Southwest Newfield Parkway outside Citrus Grove Elementary School, answering years of safety concerns from parents who say the current 45 mph speed limit puts children at risk. Many families who live in the Canopy Creek community across the street from the school walk their children to class each morning and afternoon, crossing the busy roadway.

Kelly Ribaudo, the school's PTA president and Martin County PTA Advocacy Chair, said she has spent the last five years asking the county to install a school zone. "We've had so many near misses with the kids just from people not paying attention," Ribaudo said. "Everyone has a right to a free and public education and they should be safe getting there. Our main priority should be the kids not the traffic." Parent Kendall George said the current traffic conditions frighten her. "It scares me," George said. "These cars are driving 45 miles an hour plus."

At a previous Martin County Commission meeting, commissioners sided with the parents. "Whatever the number is there is no price to someone getting hurt," Commissioner Edward Ciampi said. "You will absolutely get a school zone." School Principal Rose Rynca said the need has grown as new communities bring more students to the area. "The amount of students crossing Newfield Parkway has definitely increased," Rynca said. "This speed zone is going to really really improve the safety of students." George said a school zone sign will help alert drivers. "It's letting drivers know that, hey there's a school here, there's children crossing, and we have to slow down," George said.

A timeline for when the school zone will actually go in on Southwest Newfield Parkway has not been pinned down by the county. Until then, Ribaudo is urging drivers to use caution near the school regardless of posted signage. "Slow down if you see a school, even if there's not a school zone sign, slow down," Ribaudo said. With the school zone approved, parents say their next priority is pushing the county for better street lighting along the corridor.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Killed After Semi-Truck Turns Into SUV's Path
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after a semi-truck turned into the path of his SUV in unincorporated Indian River County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened around 6:45 a.m. at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street.

Troopers said a Freightliner semi-truck was attempting a left turn from a stop sign at westbound 49th Street onto 66th Avenue when it entered the path of a northbound Dodge Durango traveling in the inside lane. That section of 66th Avenue had no traffic controls at the intersection. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the semi-trailer, and both vehicles came to rest at the scene.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead just after 8 a.m. The Freightliner's driver, a 59-year-old Jacksonville man, was not injured. The crash remains under investigation by FHP.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee After Hazing Scandal
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against him. The decision comes two months after five firefighters were displaced for allegedly turning a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and using it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident.

The board appointed Paul Langel as interim chief following the vote. Langel, a familiar face in the district with 30 years of experience, said he views the board's decision as the end of one chapter and the start of another. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job," Langel said. "Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process."

One of the terminated firefighters, Jordon Hutchinson, called the board's vote to fire Lee a step in the right direction. "I think it was a step in the right direction," Hutchinson said. "I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department." The disciplined firefighters have said their terminations amounted to retaliation for complaints they had previously filed against district leadership.

Langel was asked whether the fired firefighters could eventually get their jobs back. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen," he said. "I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics." Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation tied to the early end of his contract. The underlying question of discipline for the firefighters involved in the bug-zapper incident remains unresolved as Langel settles into his interim role.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Chief Jeff Lee Terminated; Deputy Chief Langel Named Interim
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District board voted Wednesday to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, ending his tenure after months of turmoil over a hazing investigation and mounting criticism of district leadership. Lee did not attend the heated meeting where commissioners made the decision.

In a statement issued Thursday to a reporter, Lee pointed to improvements he said he delivered during his time leading the district. The Fire District itself noted in an October 9 statement that from 2023 to 2026 the district saw approximately 19% average pay-plan growth, an increase of about 100 uniformed personnel, and improved minimum engine staffing from two to three firefighters. The district also said it expanded employee benefits, increased retirement-health contributions, and invested in additional training, equipment and facilities. "That's really all I have to say," Lee told the reporter.

Lee's exit follows fallout from videos showing probationary firefighters being shocked with a modified bug zapper, conduct a third-party investigator concluded amounted to hazing. Three veteran firefighters were fired after that investigation, sparking backlash from firefighters, their families and community members who said the punishment was too harsh. "Not only have they lost their jobs, but they lost their reputation," one speaker told the board Wednesday. Lee's departure also came after the firefighters union delivered an overwhelming vote of no confidence in district leadership, though board member and St. Lucie County Commissioner Jamie Fowler said that vote was not the sole reason for his removal. "At the end of the day, it's gotten very messy," Fowler said. "It's not about one single decision that he's made. It's about bringing peace and calm and respect." Lee had previously signaled in a letter to the board that his time as chief could be ending, writing that the position "requires confidence" and raising the possibility of a mutually agreeable retirement.

Deputy Chief Paul Langel has been appointed interim fire chief while the district searches for a permanent replacement. "Personally, I don't think there is a culture problem," Langel said, adding he plans to visit fire stations and talk with employees individually and in groups to assess morale before deciding on next steps. Commissioners plan to hire a headhunter to search for a permanent chief both inside and outside the district, according to Fowler. The district and firefighters union are expected to keep discussing possible reinstatement of the three fired firefighters, with union representative Ryan Sapp saying he is eager to see the sides "come back together." The board is also working with an outside law firm to overhaul complaint policies after a September 30 meeting identified what members called "a significant gap" in existing procedures. Commissioner James Clasby said Lee's contract terms could leave taxpayers responsible for more than $350,000 in severance, and he wants the next chief's contract written to avoid similar terms. "That's the consequences of firing somebody with those terms," Clasby said.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man, 60, Killed in Crash With Semi at 66th Avenue and 49th Street
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. The Florida Highway Patrol said a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was attempting to turn left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified as of the report. The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner reported no injuries.

The Florida Highway Patrol's traffic homicide investigation into the crash is ongoing.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee After Hazing Scandal
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted 4-3 to terminate Fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, ending months of controversy that included hazing allegations and a no-confidence vote against his leadership. The board also appointed Paul Langel, who has 30 years of experience in the district, as interim chief.

The termination comes two months after five firefighters were displaced following allegations that they turned a bug zapper into a makeshift taser and used it to shock coworkers. Videos appear to show the alleged hazing, and three firefighters ultimately lost their jobs over the incident. Those disciplined firefighters have called their termination retaliation for complaints they previously filed against district leadership.

Langel said he sees his role now as moving the department forward. "I believe that the fire board moved forward and that was their job. Now my job is going to be to step in and start the healing process," he said. Asked whether the three terminated firefighters could get their jobs back, Langel did not rule it out. "I believe that there's always scenarios that would unfold and happen. I've got to get in and get up to speed on all the specifics," he said.

Jordon Hutchinson, one of the three terminated firefighters, said he welcomed the board's decision to remove Lee. "I think it was a step in the right direction. I don't think today was about us by any means. I think it was the best thing for the entire department," he said. Because Lee was terminated without cause, he is entitled to compensation as his contract ends early. The question of whether Hutchinson and the other two terminated firefighters will be reinstated remains unresolved as Langel settles into his new role.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Nuclear Plant Marks 50 Years as NRC Grants 20-Year License Extension
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Nuclear Power Plant, which supplies 11 percent of Florida Power & Light's power, celebrates five decades of operation after federal regulators approved another 20 years of licensing.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Nuclear Power Plant is marking 50 years of operation this year, and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission has granted licenses allowing the facility to keep running for another 20 years. The plant provides 11 percent of Florida Power & Light's total power generation. News crews were given rare access inside the facility to see how it operates and to speak with the employees who keep it running.

Carlos Santos, site vice president, explained the basic process behind the plant's power generation. "The simplest way to put it is the reactor creates the heat," Santos said. That heat comes from nuclear fission involving uranium pellets stacked into rods inside the plant's two reactor units. The heat from the rods builds up and produces steam, which flows into a secondary closed system to a turbine that generates power sent out to the electrical grid.

In August, the plant was manually shut down after three control rods dropped into the reactor core. Florida Power & Light said at the time there was no danger to staff or the public and that no customers lost power as a result.

Over five decades, technology at the plant has transformed how employees do their jobs. Nicholas Negron, associate innovation specialist, demonstrated a robotic dog named Tritium, part of a fleet of robots named after nuclear isotopes. "We're utilizing the robot to go in and out of high radiation areas, increasing efficiency both around our heavy machinery and around the plant," Negron said. The plant also uses submersibles and drones to inspect equipment. "Not only does that increase a lot of the time saving, but it's also substantial cost savings for potential materials," Negron said.

Alfred Phillips, a digital INC specialist who has worked at the plant for nearly 20 years, calibrates equipment used to maintain the systems that control the reactor, ensuring everything meets government standards and accuracy requirements. "You have million-dollar homes right down the street. We're here, but yet we're still invisible because what we do, we do it well," Phillips said. His son, Alfred Sinclair Phillips, followed him into the industry and now works in the plant's operations department. "There's a pressure with it, but there's also a sense of pride," the younger Phillips said. "Knowing that my dad has worked his butt off and he's left an impact with the people here on his work to make this place better." The elder Phillips said he takes pride in the responsibility of his daily work. "You think about all the things in life you can be doing and this is good," he said.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Now Say Two Vehicles Struck Man in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run
cards.teaser: Investigators now believe a 63-year-old man was hit by two separate vehicles near Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard, and police are asking the public to help identify both.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police are now investigating whether a 63-year-old man was struck by two separate vehicles in an Oct. 9 hit-and-run crash that left him with severe injuries. Detectives previously believed one vehicle was involved, but now say the man may have been hit by a vehicle traveling northbound and another traveling southbound near Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard.

The crash happened at about 12:56 a.m. The man was found unconscious in the roadway with severe head injuries and was taken to HCA Florida Lawnwood Hospital in critical condition.

Investigators are working to identify both vehicles and their drivers. Police have shared images of the vehicles and are asking anyone who recognizes them, witnessed the crash, or has dashcam or other video from the area to call the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

hero.headline: Veterans Day Golf Fundraiser Comes to Hobe Sound's Lost Lake Club
hero.body:
Tee It Up for the Troops will bring its Veterans Day golf fundraiser to The Club at Lost Lake in Hobe Sound for the first time this year. The tournament is scheduled for Wednesday, Nov. 11, at the club, located at 8300 SE Fazio Drive. The field is capped at 106 golfers, with registration priced at $750 per player, and local veterans paired into foursomes will play for free.

Chris LaRocque, president and executive director of Tee It Up for the Troops, said the cause is personal. "It's very close to my heart," LaRocque said in an interview with ARC Florida. "I'm an Army Reserve major myself." LaRocque said the nonprofit has deployed more than $20 million and supported more than 400,000 veterans through programs that help with the transition to civilian jobs and provide support for post-traumatic stress disorder and traumatic brain injuries.

Proceeds from the Hobe Sound tournament will also benefit local veterans programs, including PGA HOPE in South Florida, according to LaRocque. PGA HOPE introduces veterans and active-duty service members to golf as a way to support their physical, mental, social and emotional well-being.

Registration and event information for the tournament are available through Tee It Up for the Troops.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Dies After Semi-Truck Turns Into His SUV in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday morning after a semi-truck turned into the path of his SUV at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in unincorporated Indian River County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The crash happened around 6:45 a.m. when a Freightliner semi-truck attempted a left turn from a stop sign at westbound 49th Street onto 66th Avenue. A Dodge Durango was traveling north in the inside lane of 66th Avenue, which had no traffic controls at the intersection, when the semi-truck entered its path. cards.headline: Prosecutors Drop Child Abuse Case Against Indian River County Bus Driver
cards.teaser: The State Attorney's Office declined to file charges against a Sebastian school bus driver accused of grabbing and threatening to break a student's finger. The decision closes a case that began with an August surveillance video from a school bus.
cards.body:
Prosecutors have dropped the child abuse case against an Indian River County school bus driver accused of grabbing a student and threatening to break the child's finger. The State Attorney's Office filed a no information in the case against Tracy Marie Alpy on Oct. 5, according to a court document.

Alpy, 65, of Sebastian, was arrested Sept. 10 after investigators reviewed surveillance video from a school bus. The alleged incident happened Aug. 24 as the bus was transporting students to after-school care. According to an arrest affidavit, the video was recorded from 3:44 to 4:31 p.m. and showed the bus waiting at Liberty Magnet School for another bus to exchange children headed to the Gifford Youth Aquatic Center and the Boys & Girls Club.

Investigators said a student seated near the front of the bus repeatedly got out of the seat, and Alpy was seen walking through the aisle to direct the student to sit down. The affidavit said the student also appeared to repeatedly raise a middle finger toward Alpy when her back was turned. About 15 minutes into the video, Alpy sat on the edge of the student's seat to keep the child from getting up, investigators said. After more children boarded and the bus began moving, the student stood up again and turned around to interact with other children. The affidavit said Alpy repeatedly told the student to sit down, and when the child did not comply, she pulled the bus over, left the driver's seat and approached the student.

Investigators alleged Alpy grabbed the child, forced the child back into the seat and fastened the seat belt. The affidavit said the child's middle finger was extended toward Alpy at the time. Investigators said Alpy then grabbed the student's hand, forced it into the child's lap and asked, "Do you want me to break this finger?" The student later told investigators that Alpy grabbed and bent back the child's middle finger and said she was going to break it off. The child said they were afraid during the encounter, according to the affidavit. With the no information filing, the case against Alpy is now closed.

cards.headline: Police Now Say Two Vehicles Struck Man in Port St. Lucie Hit-and-Run
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police initially believed one car struck a 63-year-old man on Oct. 9, but investigators now say a second vehicle may have also hit him, and they have released images asking for help identifying both.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police are now investigating whether two vehicles, not one, struck a 63-year-old man in a hit-and-run crash earlier this month, and they have released images of both vehicles asking for the public's help identifying them. The crash happened Oct. 9 at approximately 12:56 a.m. near the intersection of Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard. The victim, a Port St. Lucie resident, was found unconscious in the roadway suffering from severe head injuries.

In an earlier update on the investigation, police said surveillance video from a nearby business captured the incident and showed what investigators believed to be a white four-door sedan striking the man before leaving the scene without stopping. As detectives continued reviewing evidence and surveillance footage, they developed information indicating a second vehicle may also have been involved.

Detectives now believe the man may have been hit by two separate vehicles, one traveling northbound and the other traveling southbound at the time of the crash. Police are working to identify both vehicles and their drivers and have released images of the vehicles to help with that effort.

Anyone who recognizes either vehicle, was in the area at the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or surveillance video from the area is asked to contact the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee, Names Langel Interim Chief
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted Wednesday to fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy over a hazing investigation and a scathing no-confidence vote from the firefighters' union. The board then voted 4-3 to appoint Deputy Chief Paul Langel as interim chief while it searches for a permanent replacement.

The meeting was packed with firefighters, union members, retirees and residents, many of whom urged commissioners to change the district's leadership. Taylor Baldwin pointed to dozens of supporters wearing yellow shirts throughout the room. "Look at everyone wearing yellow," Baldwin told commissioners. "These are not people who want to see the fire district fail. These are people who love this department enough to stand up and beg you to save it." A resident named Katie was more critical of the board itself. "You participated in this cover-up. You protected the lies and you profoundly failed the people you are elected to serve," she said.

The controversy began this summer after a hazing investigation led the district to fire three veteran firefighters and suspend two others. The district determined the conduct amounted to hazing, while the firefighters and their union have argued it was consensual horseplay. A Fort Pierce Police Department investigation found no criminal violations, and the union is now pursuing arbitration to get the three firefighters reinstated. The dispute escalated further when IAFF Local 1377 released results of a no-confidence vote earlier this month. According to the union, 423 of its 517 dues-paying members participated, and Lee received 314 no-confidence votes against 108 confidence votes, meaning 74.23% of participants said they no longer trusted his leadership.

Lee joined the department in 1997 after serving in the U.S. Navy and became the district's 14th fire chief in May 2023. He was not present for Wednesday's meeting. Commissioners spent more than 30 minutes debating whether to fire him with or without cause before ultimately choosing to terminate him without cause, which triggers severance provisions in his contract. "I think we still have to come to the determination of what exactly the final total is of the severance," board member James Clasby said after the vote. "We will only pay what we are legally required to." Commissioner Jamie Fowler, who supported the removal, said the decision gives the district a chance at a fresh start. "I feel like a weight is lifted," Fowler said. "Firing someone is never an easy decision, regardless of all the factors that come into play. So I feel like we've sort of taken a step in the right direction." The board is moving forward with hiring outside legal counsel and discussing how it will select the district's next permanent chief. The board faced a similar decision in 2017, when it accepted then-Chief Buddy Emerson's immediate retirement after a prior union no-confidence vote and paid him severance through the end of his contract.

The video, recorded from 3:44 to 4:31 p.m., showed the bus waiting at Liberty Magnet School for another bus to exchange children headed to the Gifford Youth Aquatic Center and the Boys & Girls Club, according to the affidavit. The student also appeared to repeatedly raise a middle finger toward Alpy when her back was turned, the affidavit said. About 15 minutes into the video, Alpy sat on the edge of the student’s seat to keep the child from getting up, investigators said. After more children boarded and the bus began moving, the student again stood up and turned around to interact with other children. The affidavit said Alpy repeatedly told the student to sit down. hero.headline: St. Lucie Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee, Names Interim Leader
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted Wednesday to terminate Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy that included a hazing scandal and a firefighters' union no-confidence vote. The board also voted 4-3 to appoint Deputy Chief Paul Langel as interim chief while it searches for a permanent replacement.

The meeting was packed with firefighters, union members, retirees and residents, many of whom urged commissioners to change the district's leadership. Dozens of supporters wore yellow shirts throughout the room. Taylor Baldwin pointed to the crowd and told commissioners, "Look at everyone wearing yellow. These are not people who want to see the fire district fail. These are people who love this department enough to stand up and beg you to save it." A resident identified as Katie told the board, "You participated in this cover-up. You protected the lies and you profoundly failed the people you are elected to serve."

The controversy began this summer after a hazing investigation led to the firing of three veteran firefighters and the suspension of two others. The district determined the conduct amounted to hazing, while the firefighters and their union argued it was consensual horseplay. A Fort Pierce Police Department investigation found no criminal violations, and the union is pursuing arbitration to get the three firefighters reinstated. The dispute escalated into a no-confidence vote organized by IAFF Local 1377, in which 423 of the union's 517 dues-paying members participated. Lee received 314 no-confidence votes against 108 confidence votes, with 74.23% of participants saying they no longer had confidence in his leadership.

Lee was not present for Wednesday's meeting. He joined the department in 1997 after serving in the U.S. Navy and became the district's 14th fire chief in May 2023. Commissioners spent more than 30 minutes debating whether to fire him with or without cause before voting to terminate him without cause, which triggers the severance provisions in his contract. Board member James Clasby said after the vote, "I think we still have to come to the determination of what exactly the final total is of the severance. We will only pay what we are legally required to." Commissioner Jamie Fowler, who supported the removal, said, "I feel like a weight is lifted. Firing someone is never an easy decision, regardless of all the factors that come into play. So I feel like we've sort of taken a step in the right direction." The board is also moving forward with hiring outside legal counsel and discussing the process for selecting the district's next permanent chief. In 2017, following a similar union no-confidence vote, the board accepted then-Chief Buddy Emerson's immediate retirement and paid him severance through the end of his contract.

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man Dies After Semi-Truck Turns Into SUV's Path in Indian River County
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday morning after a semi-truck turned into the path of his SUV at an uncontrolled intersection in unincorporated Indian River County, according to the Florida Highway Patrol.

The crash happened around 6:45 a.m. at 66th Avenue and 49th Street. Troopers said a Freightliner semi-truck was stopped at a stop sign on westbound 49th Street and attempting a left turn onto 66th Avenue when it entered the path of a northbound Dodge Durango. That stretch of 66th Avenue has no traffic controls. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the semi-trailer, and both vehicles came to rest near the collision site.

The Durango's driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead just after 8 a.m. The Freightliner's driver, a 59-year-old Jacksonville man, was not injured. The crash remains under investigation.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County Fire Board Fires Chief Jeff Lee, Names Paul Langel Interim Chief
hero.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District Board voted Wednesday to fire Chief Jeff Lee without cause, capping months of controversy over a hazing scandal and a union no-confidence vote. The board's vote triggers severance provisions in Lee's contract, though the final payout has not been set. Following the termination, the board voted 4-3 to appoint Deputy Chief Paul Langel as interim chief while a search begins for a permanent replacement.

Wednesday's meeting was packed with firefighters, union members, retirees and residents, many of whom urged the board to change the district's leadership. Taylor Baldwin pointed to dozens of supporters wearing yellow shirts throughout the room. "Look at everyone wearing yellow," Baldwin told commissioners. "These are not people who want to see the fire district fail. These are people who love this department enough to stand up and beg you to save it." A resident identified only as Katie told the board its members had failed the public. "You participated in this cover-up," Katie said. "You protected the lies and you profoundly failed the people you are elected to serve."

The controversy began this summer after a district hazing investigation led to the firing of three veteran firefighters and the suspension of two others. The district determined the conduct amounted to hazing, while the firefighters and their union have argued it was consensual horseplay. A Fort Pierce Police Department investigation found no criminal violations, and the union is pursuing arbitration to get the three firefighters reinstated. The dispute escalated into a no-confidence vote organized by IAFF Local 1377. The union said 423 of its 517 dues-paying members participated, with Lee receiving 314 no-confidence votes and 108 confidence votes, meaning 74.23% of participants said they no longer had confidence in his leadership.

Lee joined the department in 1997 after serving in the U.S. Navy and became the district's 14th fire chief in May 2023. He was not present for Wednesday's meeting. Commissioners spent more than 30 minutes debating whether to fire him with or without cause before settling on termination without cause. Board member James Clasby said afterward that the severance total still needs to be determined. "We will only pay what we are legally required to," Clasby said. Commissioner Jamie Fowler, who supported the removal, said the district needed a fresh start. "I feel like a weight is lifted," Fowler said. "Firing someone is never an easy decision, regardless of all the factors that come into play. So I feel like we've sort of taken a step in the right direction." The board is also moving to hire outside legal counsel and is discussing the process for selecting the district's next permanent chief. In 2017, the board faced a similar situation after a union no-confidence vote and accepted then-Chief Buddy Emerson's immediate retirement, paying him severance through the end of his contract.

Following the vote, the board also voted 4-3 to appoint Deputy Chief Paul Langel as interim chief while the district searches for a permanent replacement.

Wednesday's meeting was packed with firefighters, union members, retirees and residents, many of whom urged the board to change the district's leadership. Dozens of supporters wore yellow shirts throughout the room. "Look at everyone wearing yellow," Taylor Baldwin told commissioners. "These are not people who want to see the fire district fail. These are people who love this department enough to stand up and beg you to save it." Another resident, Katie, was harsher in her criticism of the board. "You participated in this cover-up. You protected the lies and you profoundly failed the people you are elected to serve," she said.

The controversy began this summer after a hazing investigation led to the firing of three veteran firefighters and the suspension of two others. The district determined the conduct amounted to hazing, while the firefighters and their union argued it was consensual horseplay. A Fort Pierce Police Department investigation found no criminal violations, and the union is now pursuing arbitration to get the three firefighters reinstated. The dispute escalated earlier this month when IAFF Local 1377 released the results of a no-confidence vote, in which 423 of the union's 517 dues-paying members participated. Lee received 314 no-confidence votes and 108 confidence votes, with 74.23% of participants saying they no longer had confidence in his leadership.

Lee, who joined the department in 1997 after serving in the U.S. Navy and became the district's 14th fire chief in May 2023, was not present for Wednesday's meeting. Board member James Clasby said after the vote that the exact severance amount still needs to be determined. "We will only pay what we are legally required to," he said. Commissioner Jamie Fowler, who supported Lee's removal, said the decision marks a turning point for the district. "I feel like a weight is lifted," Fowler said. "Firing someone is never an easy decision, regardless of all the factors that come into play. So I feel like we've sort of taken a step in the right direction." The board is also moving forward with hiring outside legal counsel and discussing the process for selecting the district's next permanent chief. The situation echoes 2017, when the board accepted then-Chief Buddy Emerson's immediate retirement after a prior union no-confidence vote and paid him severance through the end of his contract.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Police Now Seek Second Vehicle in Oct. 9 Hit-and-Run
cards.teaser: Investigators now believe two vehicles, traveling in opposite directions, may have struck a 63-year-old man near Northwest University and Northwest California boulevards. Police released new vehicle images and are asking the public for tips.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie Police are investigating a hit-and-run crash that seriously injured a 63-year-old man earlier this month and now believe a second vehicle may have also struck him. Detectives originally said a white four-door sedan hit the man near the intersection of Northwest University Boulevard and Northwest California Boulevard before fleeing the scene. Investigators now believe a second vehicle may have also been involved.

The crash happened at approximately 12:56 a.m. on Oct. 9. The victim, a Port St. Lucie resident, was found unconscious in the roadway suffering from severe head injuries. Surveillance video from a nearby business captured the incident and showed what investigators believed to be a white four-door sedan striking the man and leaving without stopping.

As detectives continued reviewing evidence and surveillance footage, they developed information indicating a second vehicle may also have struck the victim. Police said one vehicle was traveling northbound while the other was traveling southbound at the time of the crash. Investigators are now working to identify both vehicles and their drivers and have released images of the vehicles to the public.

Port St. Lucie Police are asking anyone who recognizes either vehicle, was in the area at the time of the crash, witnessed the incident, or has dashcam or surveillance video from the area to come forward. Tips can be submitted by calling the Port St. Lucie Police Department at 772-871-5000.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Mayor's Race and Trash Pickup Question Head to Voters
cards.teaser: Early voting is underway in Port St. Lucie, where incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin faces challenger Steven Giordano in a bitter race that also includes a non-binding ballot question on twice-weekly trash pickup.
cards.body:
Early voting began this week in St. Lucie County, giving residents their first chance to cast ballots in a Port St. Lucie mayoral race that has turned into one of the city's most contentious in recent memory. Incumbent Mayor Shannon Martin is running for another term and says the city should stay on its current path, pointing to infrastructure repairs, including roadwork, as evidence her administration is delivering results. Her opponent, Steven Giordano, argues that City Hall is corrupt and has lost touch with everyday residents. When asked what he would change, Giordano also focused on roadwork, saying the city needs a new traffic study.

At a polling location on Rosser Blvd on the first day of early voting, campaign tents for both candidates stood side by side, reflecting the sharp divide between them. Mayors in Port St. Lucie serve four-year terms and hold significant power under the city's mayor-council form of government, making this race a pivotal one for the city's direction. Candidates for mayor do not run under a political party label.

The ballot also includes a non-binding question asking voters whether Port St. Lucie should move to twice-a-week trash collection. FCC is the company that currently handles garbage pickup in the city, and switching to a second collection day would cost residents more than a hundred dollars a year in added fees. The question will not force any change on its own. City council members can choose to act on the results or disregard them entirely.

The trash issue has drawn heated reactions at recent city council meetings, where residents have criticized the current service as inadequate and pushed for an additional pickup day each week. Despite that frustration, residents approached about the issue on the first day of early voting said they would rather keep the current single pickup schedule. Resident Rob Buske summed up that sentiment, saying, "I don't want to pay for something I don't need." With the election less than two weeks away, Port St. Lucie voters are weighing both who should lead the city and how their trash gets picked up, two questions that have proven just as personal as they are practical.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Man Out on Cocaine Bond Arrested on Child Abuse Charge
cards.teaser: Nelson M. Clark was already free on bond from a cocaine possession arrest when Fort Pierce police charged him with lewd or lascivious abuse of a victim under 18.
cards.body:
Fort Pierce police arrested Nelson M. Clark, 39, on Monday, Oct. 19, on a charge of lewd or lascivious offense involving a victim under the age of 18. Clark was already out of jail on bond at the time, stemming from an arrest last month on a cocaine possession charge, according to the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Police said officers responded to a residence in the 3100 block of Avenue F at 8:34 a.m. Monday after a report of child abuse. The department's investigation led to Clark's arrest on the lewd or lascivious charge.

Clark was booked into the St. Lucie County jail on $50,000 bail.

cards.headline: Red Flag Warnings, 4-6 Foot Surf Keep St. Lucie Beaches on High Hazard Alert
cards.teaser: Dangerous surf and rip current risk are prompting St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue to urge swimmers toward lifeguarded beaches like Pepper Park and Waveland Beach.
cards.body:
A red flag warning was in effect this week at Fort Pierce Inlet State Park and other St. Lucie County beaches, where waves between four and six feet crashed along the shoreline Wednesday. The high hazard conditions are tied to a low pressure system sitting off the eastern U.S. coast in the mid-Atlantic.

St. Lucie County Ocean Rescue says the rough surf makes it more important than ever for swimmers to stick to lifeguarded beaches, pointing specifically to Pepper Park and Waveland Beach. Officials say both locations will likely be flying red or double red flags over the next few days as the hazardous conditions continue.

The county warns that rip currents are possible in these conditions. Ocean Rescue advises anyone caught in a rip current not to panic and to swim parallel to the shoreline until free of the current.

The choppy water has still drawn surfers into the waves. Foil surfer Lisa Rose described the challenge of the conditions. "It was very windy and very choppy and it's really challenging because you have to negotiate all of the chop," she said. Surfer Jodi Riley said she only went in as far as her waist. "I went in, not with my surfboard, but like, to my waist and it's just, it's rough and it's just not super safe for like, I'm sort of a beginner so not safe for me, but like, some of the other surfers have definitely been out," Riley said. Fort Pierce resident Lee Bertucelli also ventured into the water but kept his distance from the deeper surf. "I went in, you know, not too far. The waves were fun, but again not too far, didn't want to deal with rip tides or anything else," Bertucelli said. Describing the sea itself, Bertucelli added, "The sea was angry today my friends."

hero.headline: Vero Beach Man, 60, Dies in Crash With Semi at 66th and 49th
hero.body:
A 60-year-old Vero Beach man died Thursday after the SUV he was driving collided with a semi-trailer at the intersection of 66th Avenue and 49th Street in Indian River County. According to a Florida Highway Patrol crash report, a 2026 Freightliner truck-tractor pulling a flatbed trailer was turning left from a stop sign on westbound 49th Street when it entered the path of a northbound 2006 Dodge Durango traveling on 66th Avenue. The front of the Durango struck the left side of the trailer.

The Durango driver was taken to Health First's Holmes Regional Medical Center in Melbourne, where he was pronounced dead at 8:02 a.m. His next of kin had not been notified, according to the report.

The 59-year-old Jacksonville man driving the Freightliner reported no injuries.
